.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r5/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:9-11 (check 1 verify/defect) and the block-A neighbours 13-35 for scope boundaries
evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person product ask from a recruiting team, not a spec sheet or recipe. Line 1 is 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' and it frames the hard problem in the user's own terms: 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Lines 3-9 describe needs as lived experience, not as acceptance items. Examples: 'If a move is refused, put the card back where it really is and tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who.' 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none.' 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor.' 'They must never see our internal notes, why someone was rejected, or anyone else.' A grep for list/spec markers (numbered items, bullets, tables, 'shall') found none. 'must' appears only in natural sentences (lines 9 and 13). The defect patterns in quality-checks.md:11 are absent: no numbered acceptance list, no shall/must table, no feature matrix, no endpoint list and no file layout. Line 13 does name Node.js/Express/SQLite, /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH and no package installs. That is the mandatory runtime contract that check 4 requires the brief to state, and it mirrors the template-controlled integration.md (identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template/environment/instructions/integration.md). Line 13 explicitly leaves design to the builder: 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' Line 11 says 'layout and names are yours', so the brief is not a build recipe. The detailed policy is delegated to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, the house pattern (the template ships environment/instructions/ notes). That note is a policy document that uses some tables, bullets and status codes (401/403/404/409, rules.md:21-23,78). It reads as the team's working rules, not a step-by-step build recipe, and it says 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours' (rules.md:3-5). Its voice and spec density belong to check 2 (notes voice) and checks 5/6. They do not decide whether the prompt itself is a natural product request. Counterexample attempt: no plausible weak app or conforming alternative changes this row's outcome, because the row grades the brief's wording and not app behaviour. No runtime evidence is needed or missing for this row. Strength: the brief says why the product exists and what pain it must avoid (concurrent edits trampling work), which a spec sheet would not.
